name: Pushpavananathar Temple, Poovanur
deity: Shiva as Pushpavananathar (Chaturanga Vallabha Nathar), with the goddess Karpagavalli
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Poovanur, between Kumbakonam and Mannargudi in the Tiruvarur delta, honours Shiva as Pushpavananathar — the Chaturanga Vallabha Nathar — with the goddess Karpagavalli. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Appar and Sambandar, it is the 'flower-forest' shrine, where the lord and Uma are said to have chosen a flowering spot to settle.

sections.history: Poovanur lies between Kumbakonam and Mannargudi, near Needamangalam, on the northern bank of the Kaveri country, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, praised in the Tevaram by Tirunavukkarasar (Appar) and Sambandar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later, keeping the form of the Shiva shrines of the Tiruvarur delta.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Pushpavananathar — also called Chaturanga Vallabha Nathar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Karpagavalli (also named Rajarajeswari) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The walled courtyard and modest gopuram are typical of the Shiva temples of the lower Kaveri near Needamangalam.
sections.legends: The name Pushpavananathar, 'the lord of the flower-forest,' is bound to the legend that Shiva and Uma chose this flowering grove as the spot to settle, so that the place became Poovanur, the 'town of the flower-forest.' The lord is also praised as Chaturanga Vallabha Nathar. The goddess Karpagavalli stands beside him. As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims of the Kumbakonam–Mannargudi stretch include Poovanur among their stops.
sections.experience: At Poovanur the pilgrim comes to the lord of the flower-forest. Before Pushpavananathar and Karpagavalli, in the green delta between Kumbakonam and Mannargudi, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple, and the memory of the flowering grove the lord and Uma chose.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Poovanur lies between Kumbakonam and Mannargudi, near Needamangalam, in Tiruvarur district. Needamangalam and Mannargudi are the nearest towns, with buses and taxis to the village; Tiruvarur and Kumbakonam are the nearest rail heads.
